setup.description: Fixture repo`): libgit2 in a fresh temp dir, one committed file tracked.txt = 'original\n' (message 'initial').

steps: overwrite tracked.txt on disk with 'edited\n', without staging
create directory nested/ and write nested/new.txt = 'brand new\n' (untracked file inside a brand-new untracked directory)
cases.notes: tracked.txt is force-checked-out from the index (which still holds 'original\n' since nothing was staged) back over the unstaged edit. nested/new.txt is untracked so it is deleted from disk directly; the now-empty nested/ directory it lived in is also removed by discard_all_changes's walk-up-while-empty cleanup, so the directory itself must not survive either — this is the untracked-directory-cleanup behaviour, not a side effect of git itself (git never tracks empty directories, but this app's discard also removes the emptied directory to avoid leaving a stray empty folder in the file tree).

setup.description: Same base fixture as discard-all-reverts-tracked-removes-untracked: tracked.txt = 'original\n' committed.

steps: overwrite tracked.txt on disk with 'staged version\n' and stage it (index.add_path + index.write)
overwrite tracked.txt on disk again with 'unstaged version\n', on top of the staged content, without re-staging
cases.notes: discard_all_changes restores tracked.txt from the current INDEX (which holds 'staged version\n'), not from HEAD (which holds 'original\n') — so only the second, unstaged edit is rolled back; the staged edit survives untouched, both on disk and in the index. This is the GIT-012 guarantee that staged-only changes are never touched by discard-all: after discard, libgit2 reports is_index_modified() true (still staged relative to HEAD) and is_wt_modified() false (working tree now matches the index exactly).
